## apps/web/src/app/shared/ui/autocomplete.component.ts

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, input, output, signal } from '@angular/core';

export interface AutocompleteOption {
  value: string;
  label: string;
  hint?: string;
}

@Component({
  selector: 'na-autocomplete',
  standalone: true,
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <div class="ac" (focusout)="onBlur()">
      <label class="na-label" [attr.for]="inputId()">{{ label() }}</label>
      <input
        class="na-input"
        [id]="inputId()"
        type="text"
        role="combobox"
        aria-autocomplete="list"
        [attr.aria-expanded]="open()"
        [attr.aria-controls]="inputId() + '-list'"
        [placeholder]="placeholder()"
        [value]="text()"
        [disabled]="disabled()"
        (input)="onInput($event)"
        (focus)="open.set(true)"
      />
      @if (open() && filtered().length) {
        <ul class="ac__list" [id]="inputId() + '-list'" role="listbox">
          @for (option of filtered(); track option.value) {
            <li role="option" [attr.aria-selected]="option.value === text()">
              <button type="button" class="ac__option" (mousedown)="pick(option)">
                <span class="ac__value">{{ option.label }}</span>
                @if (option.hint) { <span class="ac__hint">{{ option.hint }}</span> }
              </button>
            </li>
          }
        </ul>
      }
    </div>
  `,
  styles: `
    .ac { position: relative; }
    .ac__list {
      position: absolute; top: 100%; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 50;
      background: var(--na-surface-raised); border: 1px solid var(--na-border);
      border-radius: var(--na-radius-md); box-shadow: var(--na-shadow-md);
      list-style: none; margin: var(--na-space-1) 0 0; padding: var(--na-space-1); max-height: 260px; overflow-y: auto;
    }
    .ac__option {
      width: 100%; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--na-space-3); align-items: baseline;
      background: none; border: none; text-align: left; padding: var(--na-space-2) var(--na-space-3);
      border-radius: var(--na-radius-sm); min-height: 44px;
    }
    .ac__option:hover, .ac__option:focus-visible { background: var(--na-blue-100); }
    .ac__value { font-weight: var(--na-font-medium); }
    .ac__hint { color: var(--na-ink-500); font-size: var(--na-text-xs); }
  `,
})
export class NaAutocomplete {
  readonly inputId = input(`ac-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`);
  readonly label = input.required<string>();
  readonly placeholder = input('');
  readonly options = input<AutocompleteOption[]>([]);
  readonly disabled = input(false);
  readonly selected = output<AutocompleteOption>();
  readonly query = output<string>();

  readonly text = signal('');
  readonly open = signal(false);
  readonly filtered = signal<AutocompleteOption[]>([]);

  onInput(event: Event): void {
    const value = (event.target as HTMLInputElement).value;
    this.text.set(value);
    this.query.emit(value);
    const q = value.toLowerCase();
    this.filtered.set(
      this.options().filter((o) => o.label.toLowerCase().includes(q) || o.value.toLowerCase().includes(q)),
    );
    this.open.set(true);
  }

  pick(option: AutocompleteOption): void {
    this.text.set(option.label);
    this.open.set(false);
    this.selected.emit(option);
  }

  onBlur(): void {
    setTimeout(() => this.open.set(false), 150);
  }
}

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, input, output } from '@angular/core';

export type ButtonVariant = 'primary' | 'cta' | 'secondary' | 'ghost' | 'danger';
export type ButtonSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg';

@Component({
  selector: 'na-button',
  standalone: true,
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    <button
      [type]="type()"
      [disabled]="disabled() || loading()"
      [class]="'btn btn--' + variant() + ' btn--' + size()"
      [attr.aria-busy]="loading() || null"
      (click)="clicked.emit($event)"
    >
      @if (loading()) {
        <span class="btn__spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span class="na-visually-hidden">Loading</span>
      }
      <ng-content />
    </button>
  `,
  styles: `
    .btn {
      display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: var(--na-space-2);
      border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--na-radius-md);
      font-weight: var(--na-font-semibold); min-height: 44px;
      transition: background var(--na-motion-fast) var(--na-ease), border-color var(--na-motion-fast) var(--na-ease), color var(--na-motion-fast) var(--na-ease);
    }
    .btn--sm { padding: 0.35rem 0.8rem; font-size: var(--na-text-sm); min-height: 36px; }
    .btn--md { padding: 0.55rem 1.1rem; font-size: var(--na-text-base); }
    .btn--lg { padding: 0.8rem 1.6rem; font-size: var(--na-text-lg); }
    .btn--cta { background: var(--na-cta); color: var(--na-cta-contrast); }
    .btn--cta:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--na-cta-hover); }
    .btn--primary { background: var(--na-blue-600); color: var(--na-on-accent); }
    .btn--primary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--na-blue-500); }
    .btn--secondary { background: transparent; color: var(--na-ink-900); border-color: var(--na-border-strong); }
    .btn--secondary:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--na-navy-300); background: var(--na-surface-sunken); }
    .btn--ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--na-blue-600); }
    .btn--ghost:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--na-blue-100); }
    .btn--danger { background: var(--na-danger-solid); color: #fff; }
    .btn--danger:hover:not(:disabled) { filter: brightness(0.92); }
    .btn:disabled { opacity: 0.55; }
    .btn__spinner {
      width: 1em; height: 1em; border-radius: 50%;
      border: 2px solid currentColor; border-top-color: transparent;
      animation: na-spin 0.7s linear infinite;
    }
    @keyframes na-spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .btn__spinner { animation: none; } }
  `,
})
export class NaButton {
  readonly variant = input<ButtonVariant>('primary');
  readonly size = input<ButtonSize>('md');
  readonly type = input<'button' | 'submit'>('button');
  readonly disabled = input(false);
  readonly loading = input(false);
  readonly clicked = output<MouseEvent>();
}

## apps/web/src/app/shared/ui/data-table.component.ts

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, input, output } from '@angular/core';
import type { StatusTone } from '../../core/status-maps';
import { NaSkeleton } from './skeleton.component';
import { NaEmptyState } from './empty-state.component';
import { NaBadge } from './badge.component';

export interface BadgeCell {
  text: string;
  tone: StatusTone;
}

export interface TableColumn<T = Record<string, unknown>> {
  key: string;
  label: string;
  /** hide on mobile when 'low' priority */
  priority?: 'high' | 'low';
  /** render the cell as a status badge instead of plain text */
  badge?: (row: T) => BadgeCell | null;
}

@Component({
  selector: 'na-data-table',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [NaSkeleton, NaEmptyState, NaBadge],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  template: `
    @if (loading()) {
      <div class="table-loading"><na-skeleton [rows]="[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]" height="2.5rem" /></div>
    } @else if (rows().length === 0) {
      <na-empty-state [title]="emptyTitle()" [message]="emptyMessage()" [actionLabel]="emptyActionLabel()" (action)="emptyAction.emit()" />
    } @else {
      <div class="table-wrap">
        <table>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              @for (col of columns(); track col.key) {
                <th [class.col--low]="col.priority === 'low'">{{ col.label }}</th>
              }
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            @for (row of rows(); track trackBy()(row)) {
              <tr tabindex="0" (click)="rowClick.emit(row)" (keydown.enter)="rowClick.emit(row)">
                @for (col of columns(); track col.key) {
                  <td [class.col--low]="col.priority === 'low'" [attr.data-label]="col.label">
                    @if (col.badge) {
                      @if (col.badge(row); as cell) {
                        <na-badge [tone]="cell.tone">{{ cell.text }}</na-badge>
                      } @else {
                        ‚Äî
                      }
                    } @else {
                      {{ cellText(row, col.key) }}
                    }
                  </td>
                }
              </tr>
            }
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    }
  `,
  styles: `
    .table-wrap { overflow-x: auto; border: 1px solid var(--na-border); border-radius: var(--na-radius-lg); background: var(--na-surface-raised); }
    table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: var(--na-text-sm); }
    th { text-align: left; padding: var(--na-space-3) var(--na-space-4); font-size: var(--na-text-xs); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--na-ink-500); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--na-border); background: var(--na-surface-sunken); white-space: nowrap; }
    td { padding: var(--na-space-3) var(--na-space-4); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--na-border); vertical-align: middle; }
    tbody tr { cursor: pointer; transition: background var(--na-motion-fast); }
    tbody tr:hover { background: var(--na-blue-100); }
    tbody tr:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--na-blue-600); outline-offset: -2px; }
    tbody tr:last-child td { border-bottom: none; }
    .table-loading { padding: var(--na-space-4); }
    @media (max-width: 639px) {
      .col--low { display: none; }
    }
  `,
})
export class NaDataTable<T = Record<string, unknown>> {
  readonly columns = input.required<TableColumn<T>[]>();
  readonly rows = input.required<T[]>();
  readonly loading = input(false);
  readonly emptyTitle = input('Nothing here yet');
  readonly emptyMessage = input<string | null>(null);
  readonly emptyActionLabel = input<string | null>(null);
  readonly trackBy = input<(row: T) => unknown>((row) => (row as Record<string, unknown>)['id']);
  readonly rowClick = output<T>();
  readonly emptyAction = output<void>();

  cellText(row: T, key: string): string {
    const value = (row as Record<string, unknown>)[key];
    if (value == null) return '‚Äî';
    if (typeof value === 'object') return JSON.stringify(value);
    return String(value);
  }
}

## apps/web/src/app/shared/ui/dialog.component.ts

import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component, DestroyRef, effect, inject, input, output } from '@angular/core';
import { NaButton } from './button.component';

@Component({
  selector: 'na-dialog',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [NaButton],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  host: {
    '(document:keydown.escape)': 'onEscape()',
  },
  template: `
    @if (open()) {
      <div class="backdrop" (click)="onBackdrop()" role="presentation"></div>
      <div class="dialog" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" [attr.aria-label]="title()">
        <h3 class="dialog__title">{{ title() }}</h3>
        <div class="dialog__body"><ng-content /></div>
        <div class="dialog__actions">
          <na-button variant="secondary" (clicked)="cancelled.emit()">{{ cancelLabel() }}</na-button>
          <na-button [variant]="confirmDanger() ? 'danger' : 'primary'" (clicked)="confirmed.emit()">{{ confirmLabel() }}</na-button>
        </div>
      </div>
    }
  `,
  styles: `
    .backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: var(--na-overlay); z-index: 100; }
    .dialog {
      position: fixed; top: 50%; left: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
      background: var(--na-surface-raised); border: 1px solid var(--na-border); border-radius: var(--na-radius-lg);
      box-shadow: var(--na-shadow-lg); padding: var(--na-space-6); z-index: 101;
      width: min(480px, calc(100vw - 2rem));
    }
    .dialog__title { margin-bottom: var(--na-space-3); }
    .dialog__body { color: var(--na-ink-700); margin-bottom: var(--na-space-6); }
    .dialog__actions { display: flex; justify-content: flex-end; gap: var(--na-space-3); }
  `,
})
export class NaDialog {
  readonly open = input(false);
  readonly title = input.required<string>();
  readonly confirmLabel = input('Confirm');
  readonly cancelLabel = input('Cancel');
  readonly confirmDanger = input(false);
  readonly confirmed = output<void>();
  readonly cancelled = output<void>();

  constructor() {
    const destroyRef = inject(DestroyRef);
    effect(() => {
      document.body.style.overflow = this.open() ? 'hidden' : '';
    });
    destroyRef.onDestroy(() => {
      document.body.style.overflow = '';
    });
  }

  onBackdrop(): void {
    this.cancelled.emit();
  }

  onEscape(): void {
    if (this.open()) this.cancelled.emit();
  }
}

## apps/web/src/app/shared/ui/quantity-stepper.component.ts

import { Component, computed, input, output } from '@angular/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'na-quantity-stepper',
  template: `
    <span class="qs__label" [id]="labelId">{{ label() }}</span>
    <div class="qs__group" role="group" [attr.aria-labelledby]="labelId">
      <button
        type="button"
        class="qs__btn"
        [attr.aria-label]="'Decrease ' + label()"
        [disabled]="atMin()"
        (click)="bump(-1)"
      >‚àí</button>
      <span class="qs__count" aria-live="polite">{{ value() }}</span>
      <button
        type="button"
        class="qs__btn"
        [attr.aria-label]="'Increase ' + label()"
        [disabled]="atMax()"
        (click)="bump(1)"
      >+</button>
    </div>
  `,
  styles: `
    :host { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--na-space-1); }
    .qs__label { font-size: var(--na-text-sm); color: var(--na-ink-700); }
    .qs__group { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--na-space-2); }
    .qs__btn {
      width: 40px; height: 40px; border-radius: var(--na-radius-md);
      border: 1px solid var(--na-border-strong); background: var(--na-surface-sunken);
      color: var(--na-ink-900); font-size: var(--na-text-lg); font-weight: var(--na-font-semibold);
    }
    .qs__btn:hover:not(:disabled) { border-color: var(--na-navy-300); }
    .qs__btn:disabled { opacity: 0.55; }
    .qs__count { min-width: 2ch; text-align: center; font-weight: var(--na-font-semibold); color: var(--na-ink-900); }
  `,
})
export class NaQuantityStepper {
  readonly label = input.required<string>();
  readonly value = input.required<number>();
  readonly min = input(0);
  readonly max = input(9);
  readonly valueChange = output<number>();

  protected readonly labelId = `na-qs-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`;
  protected readonly atMin = computed(() => this.value() <= this.min());
  protected readonly atMax = computed(() => this.value() >= this.max());

  protected bump(delta: number): void {
    const next = Math.min(this.max(), Math.max(this.min(), this.value() + delta));
    if (next !== this.value()) this.valueChange.emit(next);
  }
}

## apps/web/src/app/shared/ui/toast.service.ts

import { Injectable, signal } from '@angular/core';
import type { StatusTone } from '../../core/status-maps';

export interface Toast {
  id: number;
  message: string;
  tone: StatusTone;
}

@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class ToastService {
  private nextId = 0;
  readonly toasts = signal<Toast[]>([]);

  show(message: string, tone: StatusTone = 'info', durationMs = 4000): void {
    const id = this.nextId++;
    this.toasts.update((t) => [...t, { id, message, tone }]);
    setTimeout(() => this.dismiss(id), durationMs);
  }

  success(message: string): void { this.show(message, 'success'); }
  error(message: string): void { this.show(message, 'danger'); }
  info(message: string): void { this.show(message, 'info'); }
  warning(message: string): void { this.show(message, 'warning'); }

  dismiss(id: number): void {
    this.toasts.update((t) => t.filter((x) => x.id !== id));
  }
}

<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>NovaAir ‚Äî Premium Flights</title>
    <base href="/" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <script>
      (function () {
        try {
          var t = localStorage.getItem('na-theme');
          if (t !== 'light' && t !== 'dark') {
            t = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)').matches ? 'light' : 'dark';
          }
          document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', t);
        } catch (e) {
          document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
        }
      })();
    </script>
    <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="favicon.ico" />
  </head>
  <body>

*,

h3 { font-size: var(--na-text-xl); }

button {

input, select, textarea {

:focus-visible {

}

::selection {

// Screen-reader-only utility
.na-visually-hidden {
  position: absolute !important;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  margin: -1px;
  padding: 0;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0 0 0 0);

}

// Shared layout primitives
.na-container {
  max-width: var(--na-shell-max);
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 0 var(--na-space-4);
}

.na-card {
  background: var(--na-surface-raised);
  border: 1px solid var(--na-border);
  border-radius: var(--na-radius-lg);
  box-shadow: var(--na-shadow-sm);
}

.na-text-muted { color: var(--na-ink-500); }
.na-text-small { font-size: var(--na-text-sm); }
.na-text-mono { font-family: var(--na-font-mono); font-size: var(--na-text-sm); }

// Form primitives shared across screens

.na-label { font-size: var(--na-text-sm); font-weight: var(--na-font-medium); color: var(--na-ink-700); }
.na-input, .na-select {
  width: 100%;
  padding: 0.6rem 0.75rem;
  border: 1px solid var(--na-border-strong);
  border-radius: var(--na-radius-md);
  background: var(--na-surface-sunken);
  color: var(--na-ink-900);
  min-height: 44px;
  transition: border-color var(--na-motion-fast) var(--na-ease), background var(--na-motion-fast) var(--na-ease);
}
.na-input:hover, .na-select:hover { border-color: var(--na-navy-300); }
.na-input:focus-visible, .na-select:focus-visible { border-color: var(--na-ink-900); background: var(--na-surface); }
.na-input[aria-invalid='true'], .na-select[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: var(--na-danger); }
.na-input:disabled, .na-select:disabled { background: var(--na-surface-sunken); color: var(--na-ink-500); }
.na-hint { font-size: var(--na-text-xs); color: var(--na-ink-500); }
.na-error { font-size: var(--na-text-xs); color: var(--na-danger); font-weight: var(--na-font-medium); }

@media (max-width: 639px) {
  .na-container { padding: 0 var(--na-space-3); }
  // Page components set `.page { padding: <y> 0 <y> }`, whose component-scoped
  // specificity strips the container's horizontal gutter on mobile.
  // Restore the gutter inside the mobile breakpoint only; desktop is untouched.
  .na-container.na-container.page { padding-left: var(--na-space-3); padding-right: var(--na-space-3); }
  h1 { font-size: var(--na-text-2xl); }
  h2 { font-size: var(--na-text-xl); }
}

## best-practices.md

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

### Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
- Prefer Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) for new forms. They are stable in Angular v22+ and provide signal-based state, type-safe field access, and schema-based validation
- When not using Signal Forms, prefer Reactive forms instead of Template-driven ones
- Do NOT use `ngClass`, use `class` bindings instead
- Do NOT use `ngStyle`, use `style` bindings instead
- Do NOT import `CommonModule`, import only the directives and pipes the template uses, such as `AsyncPipe` or `DatePipe`
- When using external templates/styles, use paths relative to the component TS file.

## State Management

- Use signals for local component state
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Keep state transformations pure and predictable
- Do NOT use `mutate` on signals, use `update` or `set` instead

## Templates

- Keep templates simple and avoid complex logic
- Use native control flow (`@if`, `@for`, `@switch`) instead of `*ngIf`, `*ngFor`, `*ngSwitch`
- Use the async pipe to handle observables
- Do not assume globals like (`new Date()`) are available.

## Services

- Design services around a single responsibility
- Use the `providedIn: 'root'` option for singleton services
- Prefer the `@Service` decorator over `@Injectable({providedIn: 'root'})` for new singleton services (Angular v22+)
- Use the `inject()` function instead of constructor injection

## docs/KIMI_K3_IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT.md

# Prompt for Kimi K3 ‚Äî Implement the Lufthansa-Inspired Airline Booking System (SRS v2.1)

Copy everything below the line into Kimi K3 as a single prompt.

---

## Role

You are a senior full-stack engineer. Implement a **Lufthansa-inspired airline management & booking platform** according to the attached **SRS v2.1** ("Lufthansa_SRS_v2.1_Reviewed_Technical_Architecture_Added.docx"). The SRS is the single source of truth ‚Äî read it fully before writing any code, and treat every requirement as binding. This is an **educational** project: do NOT use real Lufthansa branding assets, do NOT claim real airline inventory, and mock all external integrations behind replaceable adapters.

## Technology Baseline (mandatory ‚Äî Section 19.1)

- **Frontend:** Angular (standalone components, routed feature modules, reactive forms, typed API clients, client-side validation + accessibility)
- **Backend:** NestJS (REST JSON API over HTTPS, DTO validation with class-validator, guards, interceptors, scheduled jobs)
- **Database:** PostgreSQL (transactional system of record)
- **ORM:** Prisma (only data-access layer; version-controlled migrations; explicit `@@map`/`@map` for stable SQL naming)
- **Monorepo layout:** `/apps/web` (Angular), `/apps/api` (NestJS), `/prisma` (schema + migrations), `/packages/shared` (shared DTO types if useful)
- Optional team guidance: mattpocock/skills (engineering guidance only, not a runtime dependency)

## Scope ‚Äî Two Applications, One API

### 1. Customer Web App (FR-C01 ‚Ä¶ FR-C24)
Implement every customer functional requirement, including:
- Registration, secure login/logout, **password reset / account recovery**, optional MFA (FR-C01, FR-C02, FR-C24)
- Profile management (FR-C03)
- Flight search by **trip type (one-way / round-trip / multi-city)**, origin, destination, dates, passengers, cabin class (FR-C04)
- Results with schedule **in local airport time**, duration, stops, fares, availability; filtering/sorting by price, time, duration, stops, class (FR-C05, FR-C06)
- Flight details (FR-C07)
- Passenger data collection and validation (FR-C08)
- **Seat selection with a temporary seat hold during checkout** (FR-C09 + BR-13)
- Baggage allowance + additional baggage, extras (FR-C10, FR-C11)
- Fare calculation: fare + taxes + fees + baggage + extras + discounts (FR-C12)
- Payment via **PCI DSS‚Äìcompliant provider with tokenization ‚Äî never store raw card data** (FR-C13, NFR-01)
- Unique booking reference on confirmation (FR-C14)
- My Bookings, manage booking (modify/rebook/cancel per fare rules) (FR-C15, FR-C16)
- Online check-in + digital boarding pass (FR-C17, FR-C18)
- Flight status search, baggage tracking display, notifications, loyalty balance/history (FR-C19‚ÄìFR-C22)
- Fully responsive desktop/tablet/mobile layouts (FR-C23)

### 2. Admin Dashboard (SRS Section 5.1‚Äì5.16)
Implement all sixteen admin modules with the navigation from Section 14:
Overview/analytics (totals, trends, today's flights, filters, role-aware), Flights, Airports, Aircraft (incl. seat configuration/cabin layout), Routes, Bookings (incl. **audited exception workflow** for confirming without payment), Users/Passengers, Staff, Roles & Permissions, Payments/Refunds, Baggage (incl. lost/delayed/delivered events), Check-in & Boarding, Loyalty/Miles, Notifications (templates + targeted sends + delivery status), Reports (booking/revenue/passenger/occupancy/cancellation, filterable + exportable), Audit Log (searchable, **immutable for ordinary admins**), System Settings (restricted to Super Admin/authorized roles).

## Business Rules ‚Äî enforce in the backend, not the UI (Section 8)

- **BR-01** Confirmed booking ‚áí ‚â•1 valid passenger + ‚â•1 valid flight segment
- **BR-02** One seat ‚áí one passenger per flight segment (enforce with DB uniqueness)
- **BR-03** Flight capacity never exceeded
- **BR-04 / BR-05** No confirmed booking without successful payment; payment failure never creates a confirmed booking
- **BR-06 / BR-15** Cancellation/refund/rebooking eligibility and amounts computed from configured fare rules, cancellation fees, and original payment amount
- **BR-07** Check-in only when booking + flight satisfy configured eligibility rules
- **BR-08 / BR-09** Backend-enforced RBAC on every protected operation; Super Admin has full permissions
- **BR-10 / BR-11** Audit log for sensitive actions with actor, action, target, timestamp
- **BR-12** Customers can only access their own booking/payment data
- **BR-13** Seat hold during checkout with **automatic expiry** if payment isn't completed within a configured window (Scheduler actor)
- **BR-14** Admin confirmation without successful payment only via an explicitly authorized, always-audited exception workflow

## Data Model (Section 10) ‚Äî Prisma schema + PostgreSQL

Model all 30 entities: User, Role, Permission, UserRole, RolePermission, Passenger, Airport, Route, Aircraft, Seat, **SeatHold**, Flight, FlightSegment, Fare, Booking, BookingPassenger, BookingSeat, Payment, Baggage, BaggageEvent, CheckIn, BoardingPass, ExtraService, BookingExtra, Notification, NotificationTemplate, LoyaltyAccount, LoyaltyTransaction, Refund, AuditLog, SystemSetting.

Design rules (Section 19.5):
- UUID primary keys everywhere (unless a documented external ID is required)
- Unique constraints on business identifiers: booking reference, IATA codes, loyalty member number, baggage tag number, payment provider reference
- Deliberate FK restrict/cascade behavior; **retain** booking/payment records for audit and financial traceability ‚Äî never hard-delete casually
- Seat allocation protected by active seat holds + transaction isolation + DB uniqueness
- Indexes for lookup paths (IATA codes, booking refs, seat-hold expiry queries)
- Sensitive values minimized, encrypted/tokenized, excluded from logs, with retention/deletion per GDPR-oriented NFR-10
- Migrations version-controlled; no manual production schema changes

## Architecture (Sections 11 & 19.2)

```
Customer Web App / Admin Dashboard (Angular)
        ‚Üí NestJS REST API (JSON over HTTPS)
        ‚Üí AuthN/AuthZ guards (backend is the ONLY security boundary)
        ‚Üí Domain services ‚Üí Prisma ‚Üí PostgreSQL
Backend ‚Üí Payment Provider adapter (mockable, tokenized)
Backend ‚Üí Notification Provider adapter (email/SMS, mockable)
Scheduler worker ‚Üí flight-status sync, seat-hold expiry, notification retries
```

- NestJS modules per the mapping schema (Section 19.4): `FlightsModule`, `BookingsModule`, `PaymentsModule`, `OperationsModule` (check-in + baggage), `UsersModule` (accounts, staff, RBAC, loyalty), `NotificationsModule`, `AuditModule`, plus admin-facing controllers
- Controllers validate DTOs and delegate to domain services; services never leak DB details to the frontend
- All multi-record booking / payment / seat-hold / check-in / cancellation updates use **explicit Prisma transactions**
- External integrations isolated behind interfaces so mocks can be swapped in non-production

## Non-Functional Requirements (Section 9)

- **NFR-01 Security:** bcrypt/argon2 password hashing, JWT/session hardening, input validation, no raw card storage, **rate limiting / anti-abuse on public search & booking endpoints**
- **NFR-02/03/05:** Acceptable performance, scalable modular design, graceful degradation when external providers fail
- **NFR-04/11:** Consistent booking/payment state; no duplicate confirmed bookings; referential integrity across flights, seats, passengers, bookings, payments, baggage
- **NFR-06/07:** Clear navigation, validation feedback, responsive UI
- **NFR-09:** Full auditability of security-sensitive and administrative actions
- **NFR-10:** GDPR-aligned privacy ‚Äî access control, defined retention/deletion periods
- **NFR-12:** Documented backup/recovery strategy
- **NFR-13:** Localization ‚Äî multi-language and multi-currency support on the customer platform

## Delivery Plan ‚Äî work in phases, show working software at each gate

1. **Phase 0 ‚Äî Foundation:** monorepo scaffold, Prisma schema for all 30 entities, initial migration, seed data (airports, aircraft, routes, sample flights, roles incl. Super Admin, demo users), docker-compose for PostgreSQL
2. **Phase 1 ‚Äî Identity & RBAC:** registration, login, password reset, MFA hooks, roles/permissions, guards, audit-log service
3. **Phase 2 ‚Äî Flight catalog:** airports/routes/aircraft/flights CRUD (admin) + public search with trip types, filters, sorting, rate limiting
4. **Phase 3 ‚Äî Booking core:** passenger data, seat selection with seat holds + expiry scheduler, fare calculation, payment adapter (mock provider, idempotency, tokenization), confirmation with unique booking reference
5. **Phase 4 ‚Äî Post-booking:** manage booking, cancellation/refund engine (BR-06/BR-15), check-in + boarding pass, baggage records/events, notifications
6. **Phase 5 ‚Äî Admin dashboard:** all Section 5 modules incl. reports, exports, audit-log viewer, system settings
7. **Phase 6 ‚Äî Hardening:** loyalty, localization, backup docs, E2E tests, performance pass

## Acceptance Criteria (Section 19.6 ‚Äî mandatory)

A feature is DONE only when its requirement ID traces through: use case ‚Üí Angular screen ‚Üí NestJS endpoint + service ‚Üí Prisma model/transaction ‚Üí PostgreSQL constraint/index ‚Üí automated test. In addition:

- Repository contains Prisma schema + migration history for every DB change
- DTOs, authorization guards, and service methods covered by unit/integration tests for the corresponding business rules
- **Critical booking, seat-hold, payment, cancellation, and check-in flows have E2E tests against a real PostgreSQL test database**
- Angular and NestJS module names stay aligned with the Section 19.4 mapping schema (or update the traceability doc in the same change)
- Maintain a `TRACEABILITY.md` mapping each FR/NFR/BR to its implementation and tests

## Working Agreement

- Read the full SRS first; if any requirement seems contradictory, follow the v2.1 change log resolutions (Section 18) and state your interpretation explicitly
- Never treat the Angular UI as a security boundary ‚Äî all authorization enforced in NestJS
- Mock payment/notification/flight-status providers, but keep the adapter interfaces production-shaped
- After each phase, output: what was implemented, which SRS requirement IDs it covers, test results, and known gaps
- Start with Phase 0 and Phase 1 now: produce the repo scaffold, complete Prisma schema with migrations, seed script, and the auth/RBAC foundation with tests.

Begin.

## docs/SRS_v2.1_extracted.txt

Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
Lufthansa-Inspired Airline Management & Booking System
Version 2.1 ‚Äî Full Customer Platform + Full Admin Dashboard (Reviewed & Corrected)
Academic / Software Engineering Project
1. Introduction
1.1 Purpose
This Software Requirements Specification defines the functional and non-functional requirements for a Lufthansa-inspired airline booking and management platform. The system combines a customer-facing travel platform with a full administrative dashboard through which authorized administrators can manage the major business operations of the platform.
1.2 Project Scope
The system shall support flight discovery and booking, passenger management, payments, seats, baggage, online check-in, flight status, notifications, loyalty services, and booking management. The administrative dashboard shall provide centralized management of flights, routes, airports, aircraft, users, bookings, payments, baggage, loyalty, notifications, reports, settings, staff, roles, permissions, and audit logs.
1.3 Important Project Boundary
This is a Lufthansa-inspired educational system. It is not an official Lufthansa system and shall not use private Lufthansa operational systems or claim to provide real airline inventory. Live operational data may be mocked or integrated through authorized external services.
2. System Objectives
Provide a complete and user-friendly airline booking experience.
Provide administrators with centralized control over the system.
Maintain consistent flight, booking, passenger, payment, and seat data.
Support secure authentication and role-based authorization.
Provide analytics and reports for operational decision-making.
Record important administrative and business actions through audit logs.
Provide an architecture that can scale as users, flights, and bookings increase.
3. Stakeholders and Actors
Actor
Responsibility
Guest
Searches flights and accesses public information without an account.
Customer
Registers, searches, books, pays, manages bookings, checks in, and manages profile/services.
Support Staff
Handles customer and booking support according to assigned permissions.
Flight Manager
Manages flights, schedules, routes, aircraft assignments, and operational status.
Booking Manager
Manages reservations, modifications, cancellations, and rebooking.
Finance Staff
Views transactions, payment status, refunds, and financial reports.
Administrator
Manages authorized system areas according to assigned permissions.
Super Admin
Has full system privileges and manages staff, roles, permissions, and system settings.
Payment Provider
External service that processes payment transactions.
Notification Service
External/internal service for sending email/SMS/in-app notifications.
System / Scheduler (added)
Automated background actor that executes scheduled jobs such as flight-status synchronization, seat-hold expiry, and triggered notification delivery.

5. Full Admin Dashboard Requirements
5.1 Dashboard Overview & Analytics
Display total flights, bookings, passengers, users, revenue, and occupancy indicators.
Display booking and revenue trends by selectable time periods.
Display today's flights and operational status.
Display delayed, cancelled, completed, and scheduled flights.
Display recent bookings and recent administrative activities.
Allow dashboard data to be filtered by date and other relevant dimensions.
Provide role-aware dashboard access so users only see authorized information.
5.2 Flight Management
Create, view, update, activate, deactivate, and cancel flights.
Manage flight number, origin, destination, departure, arrival, duration, status, and capacity.
Assign or change aircraft.
Manage flight schedules and rescheduling.
Manage cabin classes and fare availability.
Manage seat capacity and availability.
Prevent invalid schedules and capacity conflicts where applicable.
5.3 Airport Management
Create, view, update, activate/deactivate, and manage airports.
Maintain airport code, name, city, country, timezone, and operational status.
Associate airports with supported routes and flights.
5.4 Aircraft Management
Create, view, update, activate/deactivate, and manage aircraft.
Store aircraft model, registration/identifier, capacity, and status.
Define seat configuration and cabin layout.
Assign aircraft to flights.
5.5 Route Management
Create, view, update, activate/deactivate, and manage routes.
Define origin, destination, distance or duration metadata where required.
Associate routes with scheduled flights.
5.6 Booking Management
Search, filter, view, and manage all bookings.
View passenger, flight, fare, seat, baggage, payment, and booking-status details.
Confirm, modify, cancel, or rebook bookings according to authorized business rules.
Process or initiate refunds where permitted.
Prevent unauthorized booking modifications.
Manual confirmation of a booking without a successful payment record remains subject to BR-04 and is only permitted through an explicitly authorized exception workflow, which shall always generate an audit-log entry (new ‚Äî closes a gap between this section and BR-04).
5.7 User & Passenger Management
Search and view customer accounts.
Create, update, activate, suspend, or deactivate accounts according to permission.
View customer booking history.
Manage customer roles and account status.
View passenger information required for operational processing.
5.8 Staff, Roles & Permissions
Create and manage staff/admin accounts.
Create and manage roles.
Assign permissions to roles.
Assign roles to staff.
Support a Super Admin role with full system permissions.
Enforce authorization on the backend for every protected administrative operation.
5.9 Payments & Finance
View and search payment transactions.
Filter transactions by status, date, booking, customer, and payment method.
View successful, pending, failed, and refunded payments.
Support authorized refund operations.
Display financial summaries and revenue reports.
5.10 Baggage Management
View baggage records associated with bookings and passengers.
Manage additional baggage where supported.
Update baggage operational status.
Record lost, delayed, or delivered baggage events.
Allow authorized staff to search baggage records.
5.11 Check-in & Boarding
View passenger check-in status.
View assigned seats.
Manage eligible check-in records.
View or invalidate boarding passes according to authorized rules.
5.12 Loyalty / Miles Management
View customer loyalty accounts.
View miles/points balance and transactions.
Add or adjust loyalty transactions with proper authorization.
Configure loyalty tiers or benefits if included in the project scope.
5.13 Notification Management
Create and manage notification templates.
Send operational notifications to selected users or affected passengers.
Support booking, payment, check-in, delay, cancellation, and other configured events.
View notification delivery status when supported.
5.14 Reports
Generate booking reports.
Generate revenue/payment reports.
Generate passenger reports.
Generate flight and occupancy reports.
Generate cancellation and refund reports.
Allow date and filter-based reporting.
Allow authorized users to export reports.
5.15 Audit Log
Record important administrative and security-sensitive actions.
Store actor, action, target entity, timestamp, and relevant metadata.
Allow authorized administrators to search and filter audit logs.
Audit logs shall not be editable by ordinary administrators.
5.16 System Settings
Manage configurable system settings.
Manage supported currencies, basic booking rules, notification settings, and configurable reference data where applicable.
Restrict sensitive settings to Super Admin or explicitly authorized roles.

8. Business Rules
BR-01: A confirmed booking must reference at least one valid passenger and one valid flight segment.
BR-02: A seat cannot be assigned to more than one passenger on the same flight segment.
BR-03: A flight cannot exceed its configured passenger capacity.
BR-04: A booking cannot become confirmed unless the required payment state is successful.
BR-05: Payment failure shall not create a confirmed booking.
BR-06: Cancellation, refund, and rebooking eligibility shall follow configured fare/business rules.
BR-07: Check-in shall only be available when the booking and flight satisfy configured eligibility rules.
BR-08: Only authorized staff may perform administrative operations.
BR-09: Super Admin shall have full administrative permissions.
BR-10: Sensitive administrative actions shall create audit-log records.
BR-11: An audit log record shall identify the actor, action, target, and timestamp.
BR-12: Customer users shall not access other customers' private booking or payment information.
BR-13 (new): The system shall place a temporary hold on a selected seat during checkout to prevent concurrent double-booking; the hold shall expire automatically if payment is not completed within a configured time window.
BR-14 (new): Administrative confirmation of a booking without a successful payment record shall only occur through an explicitly authorized exception workflow, and every such exception shall generate an audit-log entry (resolves the BR-04 / Section 5.6 conflict).
BR-15 (new): Cancellation and refund amounts shall be calculated according to configured fare rules, applicable cancellation fees, and the original payment amount.
9. Non-Functional Requirements
ID
Category
Requirement
NFR-01
Security
Use secure password hashing, protected authentication, backend authorization, secure session/token handling, and input validation. Raw payment card data shall never be stored; card handling shall occur exclusively through a PCI DSS‚Äìcompliant payment provider (e.g., via tokenization). Public search and booking endpoints shall apply rate-limiting / anti-abuse protections (revised).
NFR-02
Performance
Common user and dashboard operations should provide acceptable response times under normal project load.
NFR-03
Scalability
The system architecture should support growth in users, flights, bookings, and administrative activity.
NFR-04
Reliability
Booking/payment operations shall maintain consistent state and avoid duplicate confirmed bookings.
NFR-05
Availability
The system should handle temporary failures of external services gracefully.
NFR-06
Usability
The customer and dashboard interfaces shall provide clear navigation, validation, feedback, and error messages.
NFR-07
Responsive Design
The customer-facing web application shall support desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts.
NFR-08
Maintainability
The code shall use modular architecture and separation of concerns.
NFR-09
Auditability
Security-sensitive and administrative actions shall be traceable.
NFR-10
Privacy
Personal and operational data shall be accessible only to authorized users, and shall be handled in compliance with applicable data-protection regulations (e.g., GDPR for EU customers), including defined data-retention and deletion periods (revised).
NFR-11
Data Integrity
Relationships among flights, seats, passengers, bookings, payments, and baggage shall remain consistent.
NFR-12
Backup & Recovery
The production design should provide a strategy for database backup and recovery.
NFR-13 (new)
Localization
The customer-facing platform shall support multiple languages and currencies appropriate to Lufthansa's international customer base.

11. High-Level Architecture
The implementation shall use a layered full-stack architecture. The selected baseline is Angular for the frontend, NestJS for the backend API, PostgreSQL for the relational database, and Prisma as the object-relational mapper (ORM).
Customer Web App ‚Üí Backend API ‚Üí Authentication/Authorization ‚Üí Business Services ‚Üí Database
Admin Dashboard ‚Üí Backend API ‚Üí RBAC/Permissions ‚Üí Business Services ‚Üí Database
Backend ‚Üí Payment Provider for payment operations.
Backend ‚Üí Notification Provider for email/SMS notifications where required.
12. Main Customer Flow

15. Assumptions and Constraints
The project is an educational Lufthansa-inspired system, not an official Lufthansa product.
Live flight inventory, airport operational systems, payment processing, and baggage tracking may require external APIs or mocked services.
Real-world airline policies may vary by route, fare, date, and operating carrier; project rules should therefore be configurable.
Development may initially use seeded/mock flight data.
External integrations should be isolated behind services/interfaces so they can be replaced by mocks during development.
The baseline technology stack is defined in Section 19. Any replacement technology shall preserve the stated functional, security, data-integrity, and traceability requirements.
16. Requirements Traceability
Every functional requirement should later be mapped to at least one use case, UI screen, API endpoint, database entity, and test case. This provides a traceable path from Market Research ‚Üí Requirements ‚Üí Design ‚Üí Implementation ‚Üí Testing.
17. Market Research Basis
The system scope is inspired by publicly visible Lufthansa concepts including flight search and booking, customer account services, manage-booking functions, online check-in, flight status, baggage services, and loyalty-related services. The project should validate exact current Lufthansa behavior against official public documentation before presenting any specific operational rule as a real Lufthansa requirement.
18. Version 2.1 Review ‚Äî Change Log (new)
The following gaps, contradictions, and omissions were identified in v2.0 and corrected in this version:
Added a System / Scheduler actor (Section 3) ‚Äî automated jobs (status sync, seat-hold expiry, notifications) had no owning actor.
FR-C02 & new FR-C24 ‚Äî no account-recovery (password reset) or MFA requirement existed for a system handling payment data.
FR-C04 ‚Äî flight search did not specify trip type (one-way / round-trip / multi-city).
FR-C09 & BR-13 & SeatHold entity ‚Äî no mechanism prevented two customers from concurrently booking the same seat during checkout (a real double-booking risk).
FR-C13 & NFR-01 ‚Äî no requirement barring storage of raw card data or requiring PCI DSS‚Äìcompliant payment handling.
Section 5.6 & BR-14 ‚Äî admin 'Confirm booking' capability could bypass BR-04's payment-success requirement with no stated safeguard; now scoped to an audited exception workflow.
BR-15 ‚Äî no rule governed how refund/cancellation amounts are actually calculated.
NFR-10 ‚Äî privacy requirement did not reference data-protection regulation (e.g., GDPR) or retention/deletion periods, despite Lufthansa being EU-based.
NFR-13 ‚Äî no localization requirement existed despite the platform targeting an international customer base.
NFR-01 ‚Äî no anti-abuse/rate-limiting requirement for public-facing search and booking endpoints.
19. Technical Architecture, ERD, and Mapping Schema
This section defines the implementation baseline for the requirements in this SRS. It refines the high-level architecture in Section 11 and establishes a shared contract between the Angular frontend, NestJS backend, PostgreSQL database, and Prisma data-access layer. The design is intentionally modular so that external payment, notification, and operational integrations can be mocked during development and replaced without changing the customer-facing requirements.
19.1 Technology Stack
Layer
Technology
SRS-aligned responsibility
Frontend
Angular
Customer portal and admin dashboard; routed feature modules; typed API clients; reactive forms; client-side validation and accessibility.
Backend API
NestJS
REST API, DTO validation, authentication, authorization guards, domain services, integration adapters, scheduled jobs, and audit orchestration.
Database
PostgreSQL
Transactional system of record for users, flights, bookings, payments, check-in, baggage, loyalty, notifications, settings, and audit data.
ORM / data access
Prisma
Type-safe database client, schema definition, migrations, relation queries, transaction boundaries, and generated TypeScript types.
Developer guidance
mattpocock/skills
Optional shared TypeScript and engineering guidance used by the project team during implementation and review; it is not a runtime dependency.
External integrations
Provider adapters behind NestJS interfaces
Payment, email/SMS, flight-status, and other providers remain replaceable and may be mocked in non-production environments.
19.2 Logical Application Architecture
The Angular application communicates with NestJS over HTTPS using JSON APIs. NestJS owns business rules and authorization decisions; Angular must not be treated as a security boundary. Prisma is the only application data access layer for PostgreSQL, and all multi-record booking, payment, seat-hold, check-in, and cancellation updates shall use explicit transaction boundaries. Scheduled workers are responsible for status synchronization, expiry of seat holds, notification retries, and other automated actions described in the requirements.
‚Ä¢ Angular feature areas shall be organized around search, booking, manage booking, check-in, customer profile, and administration.
‚Ä¢ NestJS modules shall isolate flights, bookings, payments, operations, users and RBAC, notifications, reporting, and audit concerns.
‚Ä¢ PostgreSQL constraints and indexes shall enforce uniqueness and lookup requirements such as IATA codes, booking references, payment provider references, and seat-hold expiry queries.
‚Ä¢ Prisma migrations shall be version-controlled and applied through the project deployment process; production schema changes shall not be made manually.
19.3 Entity Relationship Diagram
The following conceptual ERD maps the core entities already listed in Section 10 to their principal relationships. Join entities are shown explicitly for many-to-many relationships, and SeatHold is included to support the concurrency rule that prevents two customers from booking the same seat during checkout.
Figure 1. Conceptual entity relationship diagram for the Lufthansa-inspired booking platform.
19.4 Module-to-API-to-Data Mapping Schema
The mapping schema below defines the expected direction of dependencies. Angular feature modules call NestJS controllers. Controllers validate DTOs and delegate to domain services. Domain services use Prisma model groups and integration ports; they do not expose database details directly to the frontend.
Figure 2. Application module, API, domain-service, integration, and Prisma mapping schema.
Frontend capability
NestJS API module
Primary Prisma entities
Key controls
Search and flight results
FlightsModule
Airport, Route, Aircraft, Flight, FlightSegment, Fare, Seat
Validated search criteria; status and schedule filtering; pagination; rate limiting.
Booking and manage booking
BookingsModule
Booking, BookingPassenger, BookingSeat, Passenger, Fare, SeatHold, ExtraService, BookingExtra
Seat-hold transaction; fare revalidation; booking-reference authorization; immutable booking history.
Payments and refunds
PaymentsModule
Payment, Refund, Booking
Provider tokenization; no raw card storage; idempotency; payment-success gate; audited refund calculation.
Check-in and boarding
OperationsModule
CheckIn, BoardingPass, BookingPassenger, BookingSeat, Flight
Eligibility checks; one boarding pass per eligible passenger/segment; operational status validation.
Baggage services
OperationsModule
Baggage, BaggageEvent, Booking
Tag uniqueness; event history; role-based operational access; customer visibility limits.
Accounts, staff, RBAC, and loyalty
UsersModule
User, Role, Permission, UserRole, RolePermission, LoyaltyAccount, LoyaltyTransaction
Password hashing; MFA support; backend guards; least privilege; points ledger integrity.
Notifications and audit
NotificationsModule plus AuditModule
NotificationTemplate, Notification, AuditLog, SystemSetting
Retryable delivery; template versioning; actor/entity audit trail; retention policy.
19.5 Prisma and PostgreSQL Design Rules
‚Ä¢ Every persistent entity shall have a stable UUID primary key unless a documented external identifier is required for interoperability.
‚Ä¢ Natural business identifiers such as booking reference, IATA code, member number, tag number, and provider reference shall have explicit unique constraints where applicable.
‚Ä¢ Foreign keys shall use restrictive or cascading behavior deliberately. Booking and payment records shall be retained for audit and financial traceability rather than deleted casually.
‚Ä¢ Seat allocation shall be protected by a combination of active seat holds, transaction isolation, and database uniqueness rules appropriate to the booking lifecycle.
‚Ä¢ Sensitive values shall be minimized, encrypted or tokenized where required, excluded from logs, and subject to the retention and deletion requirements in the SRS.
‚Ä¢ Prisma schema names may follow project TypeScript conventions while PostgreSQL table and column mappings remain explicit through @@map and @map where a stable SQL naming convention is needed.
19.6 Traceability and Implementation Acceptance Criteria
A feature is considered technically traceable when its requirement identifier can be followed through a use case, Angular screen or workflow, NestJS endpoint and service, Prisma model or transaction, PostgreSQL constraint or index where relevant, and automated test case. This traceability path extends the requirement statement in Section 16 and shall be maintained as the implementation evolves.
‚Ä¢ The repository shall contain the Prisma schema and migration history for every released database change.
‚Ä¢ API DTOs, authorization guards, and service methods shall be covered by unit or integration tests for the corresponding business rules.
‚Ä¢ Critical booking, seat-hold, payment, cancellation, and check-in flows shall have end-to-end tests against a PostgreSQL test database.
‚Ä¢ The Angular and NestJS module names shall remain aligned with the mapping schema unless the traceability section is updated in the same change.

## prisma/migrations/migration_lock.toml

# Please do not edit this file manually
# It should be added in your version-control system (e.g., Git)
provider = "postgresql"

---
## prisma/schema.prisma

// This is your Prisma schema file,
// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
  output   = "../node_modules/.prisma/client"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

// ---------- Identity & RBAC ----------

model User {
  id             String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  email          String    @unique @db.VarChar(255)
  passwordHash   String    @map("password_hash") @db.VarChar(255)
  firstName      String    @map("first_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  lastName       String    @map("last_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  phone          String?   @db.VarChar(50)
  emailVerified  Boolean   @default(false) @map("email_verified")
  mfaSecret      String?   @map("mfa_secret") @db.VarChar(255)
  mfaEnabled     Boolean   @default(false) @map("mfa_enabled")
  mfaBackupCodes String?   @map("mfa_backup_codes") @db.Text
  resetToken     String?   @map("reset_token") @db.VarChar(255)
  resetTokenExpiresAt DateTime? @map("reset_token_expires_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  status         UserStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  createdAt      DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  updatedAt      DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  userRoles      UserRole[]
  bookings       Booking[]
  passengers     Passenger[]
  loyaltyAccount LoyaltyAccount?
  notifications  Notification[]
  auditLogs      AuditLog[]
  seatHolds      SeatHold[]

  @@map("users")
}

enum UserStatus {
  ACTIVE
  SUSPENDED
  DEACTIVATED
  PENDING_VERIFICATION

  @@map("user_status")
}

model Role {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  name        String   @unique @db.VarChar(100)
  description String?  @db.Text
  isSuperAdmin Boolean @default(false) @map("is_super_admin")
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  userRoles        UserRole[]
  rolePermissions  RolePermission[]

  @@map("roles")
}

model Permission {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  resource    String   @db.VarChar(100)
  action      String   @db.VarChar(100)
  description String?  @db.Text

  rolePermissions RolePermission[]

  @@unique([resource, action])
  @@map("permissions")
}

model UserRole {
  id     String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId String @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  roleId String @map("role_id") @db.Uuid

  user   User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  role   Role   @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@unique([userId, roleId])
  @@map("user_roles")
}

model RolePermission {
  id           String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  roleId       String @map("role_id") @db.Uuid
  permissionId String @map("permission_id") @db.Uuid

  role       Role       @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  permission Permission @relation(fields: [permissionId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@unique([roleId, permissionId])
  @@map("role_permissions")
}

// ---------- Passengers ----------

model Passenger {
  id             String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  userId         String?   @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  firstName      String    @map("first_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  lastName       String    @map("last_name") @db.VarChar(100)
  dateOfBirth    DateTime? @map("date_of_birth") @db.Date
  passportNumber String?   @map("passport_number") @db.VarChar(50)
  nationality    String?   @db.VarChar(100)
  createdAt      DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  updatedAt      DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  user              User?              @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  bookingPassengers BookingPassenger[]

  @@map("passengers")
}

// ---------- Flight catalog ----------

model Airport {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  iataCode  String   @unique @map("iata_code") @db.VarChar(3)
  icaoCode  String?  @map("icao_code") @db.VarChar(4)
  name      String   @db.VarChar(200)
  city      String   @db.VarChar(100)
  country   String   @db.VarChar(100)
  timezone  String   @db.VarChar(100)
  latitude  Decimal? @db.Decimal(10, 8)
  longitude Decimal? @db.Decimal(11, 8)
  status    AirportStatus @default(ACTIVE)

  routesOrigin      Route[]         @relation("RouteOrigin")
  routesDestination Route[]         @relation("RouteDestination")
  flightSegmentsOrigin      FlightSegment[] @relation("FlightSegmentOrigin")
  flightSegmentsDestination FlightSegment[] @relation("FlightSegmentDestination")

  @@map("airports")
}

enum AirportStatus {
  ACTIVE
  INACTIVE

  @@map("airport_status")
}

model Route {
  id                   String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  originAirportId      String @map("origin_airport_id") @db.Uuid
  destinationAirportId String @map("destination_airport_id") @db.Uuid
  distanceKm           Int?   @map("distance_km")
  durationMinutes      Int?   @map("duration_minutes")
  status               RouteStatus @default(ACTIVE)

  originAirport      Airport   @relation("RouteOrigin", fields: [originAirportId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  destinationAirport Airport   @relation("RouteDestination", fields: [destinationAirportId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  flights            Flight[]

  @@unique([originAirportId, destinationAirportId])
  @@map("routes")
}

enum RouteStatus {
  ACTIVE
  INACTIVE

  @@map("route_status")
}

model Aircraft {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  registration String @unique @db.VarChar(50)
  model      String   @db.VarChar(100)
  capacity   Int
  status     AircraftStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  seats   Seat[]
  flights Flight[]

  @@map("aircraft")
}

enum AircraftStatus {
  ACTIVE
  MAINTENANCE
  RETIRED

  @@map("aircraft_status")
}

model Seat {
  id          String     @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  aircraftId  String     @map("aircraft_id") @db.Uuid
  seatNumber  String     @map("seat_number") @db.VarChar(10)
  cabinClass  CabinClass @map("cabin_class")
  seatRow     Int?       @map("seat_row")
  seatColumn  String?    @map("seat_column") @db.VarChar(5)
  features    Json?      @db.JsonB
  isExitRow   Boolean    @default(false) @map("is_exit_row")

  aircraft    Aircraft    @relation(fields: [aircraftId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  seatHolds   SeatHold[]
  bookingSeats BookingSeat[]

  @@unique([aircraftId, seatNumber])
  @@map("seats")
}

enum CabinClass {
  ECONOMY
  PREMIUM_ECONOMY
  BUSINESS
  FIRST

  @@map("cabin_class")
}

model SeatHold {
  id        String      @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  flightId  String      @map("flight_id") @db.Uuid
  seatId    String      @map("seat_id") @db.Uuid
  userId    String?     @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  sessionId String?     @map("session_id") @db.VarChar(255)
  status    SeatHoldStatus @default(ACTIVE)
  expiresAt DateTime    @map("expires_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  createdAt DateTime    @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  flight Flight @relation(fields: [flightId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  seat   Seat   @relation(fields: [seatId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  user   User?  @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@index([status, expiresAt])
  @@index([flightId, seatId])
  @@map("seat_holds")
}

enum SeatHoldStatus {
  ACTIVE
  EXPIRED
  CONVERTED
  RELEASED

  @@map("seat_hold_status")
}

model Flight {
  id             String      @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  flightNumber   String      @map("flight_number") @db.VarChar(20)
  routeId        String      @map("route_id") @db.Uuid
  aircraftId     String      @map("aircraft_id") @db.Uuid
  departureTime  DateTime    @map("departure_time") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  arrivalTime    DateTime    @map("arrival_time") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  status         FlightStatus @default(SCHEDULED)
  scheduleStatus FlightScheduleStatus @default(ONTIME) @map("schedule_status")
  createdAt      DateTime    @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  updatedAt      DateTime    @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  route        Route          @relation(fields: [routeId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  aircraft     Aircraft       @relation(fields: [aircraftId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  segments     FlightSegment[]
  fares        Fare[]
  seatHolds    SeatHold[]

  @@index([departureTime])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("flights")
}

enum FlightStatus {
  SCHEDULED
  ACTIVE
  DELAYED
  CANCELLED
  COMPLETED

  @@map("flight_status")
}

enum FlightScheduleStatus {
  ONTIME
  DELAYED
  CANCELLED

  @@map("flight_schedule_status")
}

model FlightSegment {
  id                   String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  flightId             String   @map("flight_id") @db.Uuid
  segmentNumber        Int      @map("segment_number")
  originAirportId      String   @map("origin_airport_id") @db.Uuid
  destinationAirportId String   @map("destination_airport_id") @db.Uuid
  departureTime        DateTime @map("departure_time") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  arrivalTime          DateTime @map("arrival_time") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  flight                Flight          @relation(fields: [flightId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  originAirport         Airport         @relation("FlightSegmentOrigin", fields: [originAirportId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  destinationAirport    Airport         @relation("FlightSegmentDestination", fields: [destinationAirportId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  bookingSeats          BookingSeat[]
  checkIns              CheckIn[]

  @@unique([flightId, segmentNumber])
  @@map("flight_segments")
}

model Fare {
  id             String     @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  flightId       String     @map("flight_id") @db.Uuid
  cabinClass     CabinClass @map("cabin_class")
  basePrice      Decimal    @map("base_price") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  taxAmount      Decimal    @default(0) @map("tax_amount") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  feeAmount      Decimal    @default(0) @map("fee_amount") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  currency       String     @db.VarChar(3)
  availableCount Int        @map("available_count")
  fareRules      Json?      @map("fare_rules") @db.JsonB

  flight Flight @relation(fields: [flightId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([flightId, cabinClass])
  @@map("fares")
}

// ---------- Bookings ----------

model Booking {
  id              String        @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  bookingReference String       @unique @map("booking_reference") @db.VarChar(10)
  userId          String        @map("user_id") @db.Uuid
  status          BookingStatus @default(PENDING)
  totalAmount     Decimal       @map("total_amount") @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  currency        String        @db.VarChar(3)
  bookedAt        DateTime      @default(now()) @map("booked_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  contactEmail    String        @map("contact_email") @db.VarChar(255)
  contactPhone    String?       @map("contact_phone") @db.VarChar(50)
  fareRulesSnapshot Json?       @map("fare_rules_snapshot") @db.JsonB

  user             User              @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  bookingPassengers BookingPassenger[]
  bookingExtras    BookingExtra[]
  payments         Payment[]
  refunds          Refund[]
  notifications    Notification[]
  auditLogs        AuditLog[]

  @@index([userId, bookedAt])
  @@map("bookings")
}

enum BookingStatus {
  PENDING
  CONFIRMED
  CANCELLED
  CHECKED_IN
  BOARDED
  NO_SHOW

  @@map("booking_status")
}

model BookingPassenger {
  id            String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  bookingId     String @map("booking_id") @db.Uuid
  passengerId   String @map("passenger_id") @db.Uuid
  passengerType PassengerType @default(ADULT) @map("passenger_type")

  booking   Booking    @relation(fields: [bookingId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  passenger Passenger  @relation(fields: [passengerId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  seats     BookingSeat[]
  baggage   Baggage[]
  checkIns  CheckIn[]

  @@unique([bookingId, passengerId])
  @@map("booking_passengers")
}

enum PassengerType {
  ADULT
  CHILD
  INFANT

  @@map("passenger_type")
}

model BookingSeat {
  id                 String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  bookingPassengerId String @map("booking_passenger_id") @db.Uuid
  flightSegmentId    String @map("flight_segment_id") @db.Uuid
  seatId             String @map("seat_id") @db.Uuid
  seatNumber         String @map("seat_number") @db.VarChar(10)

  bookingPassenger BookingPassenger @relation(fields: [bookingPassengerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  flightSegment    FlightSegment    @relation(fields: [flightSegmentId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  seat             Seat             @relation(fields: [seatId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@unique([bookingPassengerId, flightSegmentId])
  @@unique([flightSegmentId, seatId])
  @@map("booking_seats")
}

// ---------- Payments & Refunds ----------

model Payment {
  id               String        @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  bookingId        String        @map("booking_id") @db.Uuid
  amount           Decimal       @db.Decimal(12, 2)
  currency         String        @db.VarChar(3)
  status           PaymentStatus @default(PENDING)
  provider         String        @db.VarChar(50)
  providerReference String?      @unique @map("provider_reference") @db.VarChar(255)
  token            String?       @db.VarChar(255)
  idempotencyKey   String?       @map("idempotency_key") @db.VarChar(255)
  paidAt           DateTime?     @map("paid_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  failedAt         DateTime?     @map("failed_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  createdAt        DateTime      @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)
  updatedAt        DateTime      @updatedAt @map("updated_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  booking  Booking   @relation(fields: [bookingId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  refunds  Refund[]

  @@index([bookingId, status])
  @@map("payments")
}

enum PaymentStatus {
  PENDING
  AUTHORIZED
  SUCCESS
  FAILED
  REFUNDED
  PARTIALLY_REFUNDED

  @@map("payment_status")
}

model Refund {
  id          String       @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  paymentId   String       @map("payment_id") @db.Uuid
  bookingId   String       @map("booking_id") @db.Uuid
  amount      Decimal      @db.Decimal(12, 2)

  createdAt   DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at") @db.Timestamptz(6)

  payment Payment @relation(fields: [paymentId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  booking Booking @relation(fields: [bookingId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@index([bookingId])
  @@map("refunds")
}

enum RefundStatus {
  PENDING
  APPROVED
  REJECTED
  PROCESSED

  @@map("refund_status")
}

// ---------- Baggage ----------

model Baggage {
  id                 String @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid

  @@map("baggage")
}

enum BaggageType {

}

enum BaggageStatus {

model BaggageEvent {

// ---------- Check-in & Boarding ----------

model CheckIn {

model BoardingPass {

model AuditLog {

model SystemSetting {
